events.title: Earliest surviving English cheque is written
events.description: Nicholas Vanacker wrote a cheque for 400 pounds drawn on his London goldsmith-bankers, Morris and Clayton. It is the oldest known surviving handwritten cheque in Britain.
events.html: Nicholas Vanacker wrote a cheque for 400 pounds drawn on his London goldsmith-bankers, Morris and Clayton. It is the oldest known surviving handwritten cheque in Britain.

events.title: Stephen Decatur burns the captured USS Philadelphia at Tripoli
events.description: Lieutenant Decatur and a small crew slipped into Tripoli harbour and set fire to the frigate, captured by the Barbary state. Nelson is said to have called it the most daring act of the age.

events.title: Howard Carter opens Tutankhamun's burial chamber
events.description: Before invited officials, Carter broke through the sealed wall to reveal a gilded shrine filling the chamber. The king's sarcophagus and gold coffins lay within, untouched for over 3,000 years.
events.html: Before invited officials, Carter broke through the sealed wall to reveal a gilded shrine filling the chamber. The king's sarcophagus and gold coffins lay within, untouched for over 3,000 years.

events.title: Wallace Carothers's nylon is patented
events.description: DuPont received the patent for nylon, invented by a team led by Wallace Carothers. The first fully synthetic fibre, it was used for stockings and then wartime parachutes.
events.html: DuPont received the patent for nylon, invented by a team led by Wallace Carothers. The first fully synthetic fibre, it was used for stockings and then wartime parachutes.

events.title: American paratroopers and infantry assault Corregidor
events.description: US forces landed by parachute and sea on the island fortress at the mouth of Manila Bay, lost in 1942. After two weeks of fighting most of its Japanese defenders were dead.
events.html: US forces landed by parachute and sea on the island fortress at the mouth of Manila Bay, lost in 1942. After two weeks of fighting most of its Japanese defenders were dead.

events.title: First 911 emergency call made in Alabama
events.description: In Haleyville, Alabama, Senator Rankin Fite made the first call on the new 911 emergency number. A single, easily remembered number spread across the United States over the following decades.
